The manipulation of time in this excerpt—the famous opening of Theodor Fontane's classic novel *Effi Briest*—is masterfully balanced to suit its narrative purpose. 

Initially, time is essentially paused (or stretched) in the first two paragraphs to provide a detailed, atmospheric description of the Hohen-Cremmen estate and to introduce the habitual, leisurely afternoon activities of Effi and her mother. This slow pacing mirrors the "mittagsstille" (midday quiet) of the setting and establishes the characters' personalities and relationship dynamics. 

The narrative then transitions smoothly into "real-time" through the lively dialogue between Effi and her mother, which captures Effi's energetic and impulsive nature. Finally, when the three friends arrive, the author uses slight time compression ("tat rasch ein paar Fragen" / quickly asked a few questions) to bypass mundane pleasantries and keep the scene moving forward at a natural, engaging rhythm.
